date_scope: Revision Guide for Family 17h Models 00h–0Fh maps to first-generation EPYC 7001/Naples. This generation also includes Threadripper products outside this server-family plotting label.
Revision Guide for Family 17h Models 30h–3Fh maps to 2nd Gen EPYC 7002/Rome.
Revision Guide for Family 19h Models 10h–1Fh maps to EPYC 9004 Genoa / 4th Gen EPYC.
Revision Guide for Family 1Ah Models 00h–0Fh maps to 5th Gen EPYC 9005 / Turin.
The update covers 8th- and 9th-generation Core desktop families. The earliest covered Coffee Lake desktop commercial availability is 8th Gen in 2017; the 9th Gen extension followed in 2018.
10th Gen U/Y mobile specification update maps to Ice Lake client, separate from the server Ice Lake-SP family.
The specification covers 11th Gen UP3/UP4/H35/H45 mobile Tiger Lake variants; Intel first introduced the mobile family in 2020.
12th Gen Intel Core is Alder Lake; the first unlocked desktop processors launched with the family introduction at Intel Innovation.
11th Gen S-series desktop processors are Rocket Lake-S, separate from 11th Gen Tiger Lake mobile.
The specification update spans 13th and 14th Gen Core. The earliest covered family launch is 13th Gen Raptor Lake in 2022; 14th Gen desktop products followed in 2023.
Intel Core Ultra mobile processors are the Meteor Lake client family in this specification update.
Intel Core Ultra Series 2 specification update maps the initial 200S desktop product family to Arrow Lake-S.
The input document covers Core Ultra 200V Series, codenamed Lunar Lake.
Intel’s Xeon E5-2600 v4 family (Broadwell-EP) is the document’s covered server product family; dated Intel investor-relations release identifies the 2016 announcement.

The specification update covers the first Xeon Scalable family, codenamed Skylake-SP; Intel’s developer overview identifies the new generation as formerly Skylake-SP and states the Xeon Scalable platform launched that year.
2nd Gen Xeon Scalable processors are Cascade Lake; this official Intel release says they were released and generally available on April 2, 2019.
The input document covers 3rd Gen Xeon Scalable (server Ice Lake), not the client Ice Lake family.
5th Gen Intel Xeon / Xeon Scalable is codenamed Emerald Rapids; this is the server product family in the input source.
4th Gen Xeon Scalable is codenamed Sapphire Rapids; the source release is the January 2023 launch notice.
